//: SECURITY_DEFINER_ORACLES.json — read by src/scripts/checkSecurityDefinerOracles.ts. Keys are bare function names in `public` that are SECURITY DEFINER and that NOTHING in the corpus references: no surviving RLS policy, no other function body, no view, no trigger, and no string literal in src/. Every entry is validated on every run: a key that is no longer a definer function FAILS, a key that has since acquired a reference FAILS, and a reason that does not begin with a classification or runs under 80 characters FAILS. This list may only shrink.
//classifications: RPC-BY-DESIGN: meant to be called over PostgREST by a client this corpus does not contain. OPERATOR-ONLY: called by hand or by a scheduler outside the repo, and its grants say so. PENDING-OWNER: its fate is an unmade product decision. HOLD: it belongs to a workstream that is deliberately frozen. DEAD: superseded, kept only because dropping it needs a migration.
//remedy: The remedy for an entry here is a DROP, or a REVOKE when no policy calls it. It is NEVER a REVOKE on a policy-referenced function: revoking EXECUTE makes the policy itself raise 'permission denied for function' for every end-user token. That was measured on the CI project for both `language sql` and `language plpgsql`; the check's header carries the transcript.

unreferenced.event_is_in_state: HOLD: an events existence-and-state oracle — EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM events WHERE id = eid AND state = ANY(states)) — defined by 2033_rls_hardening.sql as a helper for policies that were never written with it. Live grants are the widest of any entry here: anon AND authenticated both hold EXECUTE (verified 2026-09-08), so POST /rpc/event_is_in_state answers, for any event id, whether that event exists and is in a named state, to a caller who has not signed in. It is 0-referenced by 808 surviving policies. It is NOT dropped or revoked here because Event Truth Phase-B is a declared HOLD and EVENT_START_TRANSITION is an OWNER decision: this function is the shape a state-gated policy would be built from, so retiring it is a decision inside frozen work rather than a cleanup outside it. What is recorded instead is that its exposure is live and unearned TODAY, so that whoever unfreezes that workstream inherits the finding rather than rediscovering it.
unreferenced.increment_hashtag_usage_count: DEAD: superseded by upsert_hashtag_usage_and_increment, which is what TaggingService.ts actually calls and which exists specifically to stop the double-counting this one permits. Its whole body is an unconditional UPDATE hashtags SET usage_count = usage_count + 1 with no dedup, no rate limit and no check on the caller. Uncalled anywhere in the repository: the only 16 mentions are documentation tables and duplicate copies of migration 0043/0044. EXECUTE was granted to `authenticated`, which made POST /rpc/increment_hashtag_usage_count a trending-counter inflation primitive for any signed-in account — the exact guarantee its replacement was written to provide, reachable by going around it. That grant is withdrawn by migration 2551; the function itself stays until someone decides whether to drop it, because a DROP is not reversible by a grant.
unreferenced.purge_old_ranking_debug_samples: HOLD: DELETEs ranking_debug_samples older than seven days and returns the count. Uncalled in the repository — no scheduler in src/services or src/scripts names it. EXECUTE is granted to `authenticated` (verified 2026-09-08), so any signed-in account can trigger the purge; the blast radius is bounded to rows already past their intended retention, which is why this is recorded rather than treated as urgent. It is left alone because ranking_debug_samples is Ranker surface and Ranker is a declared HOLD. The grant is the part that is wrong, not the function.
unreferenced.revoke_sensing_sessions_for_profile: OPERATOR-ONLY: added by 2481_sensing_sessions_option_a_issuer.sql as the revocation half of the sensing-session issuer. Its grants already say what it is — postgres and service_role only, with neither anon nor authenticated holding EXECUTE (verified 2026-09-08) — so it is not reachable over PostgREST by a user token at all, and it is listed here only because nothing in the corpus calls it yet. SENSING_AUTH_POSTURE is an OWNER decision and the caller is on the far side of it; the function is the built half waiting for the decided half.
